title: Gideon and the Wreck
premise: Gideon Blackwood, a disgraced mountain guide fleeing a scandal she didn't cause, takes a salvage contract in a fjord town where the low tide has exposed a sea cave that local legend forbids entering. Inside she finds a drowned expedition's journal pointing to a river that runs beneath the glacier to a forbidden source — and evidence that the town's most powerful man financed that doomed expedition and will kill to keep it buried. Pursued by his hired men and shadowed by Mara, the salvager's daughter whose loyalty is torn between her town and the truth, Gideon must ascend the river to the glacier's source before the calving season seals the route for a year. She reaches the source, exposes the truth at terrible cost — Mara's father dies, the town turns on its patron, and Gideon, offered redemption she no longer trusts, walks out of the mountains alone but finally free of what she was running from.
about_author: Hazel Oyelaran is a former river-rafting instructor who spent six seasons guiding in glacial fjords before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who are better in the wild than they ever manage to be at home.

chapters.title: The Low Tide
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Broke and blacklisted, Gideon arrives in the fjord town of Skarnvik and takes a salvage contract she'd normally refuse. The lowest tide in a decade has exposed a sea cave the locals won't name. Beat: wary pragmatism masking exhaustion; she's running on momentum alone.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Inside the cave she recovers a waterproof satchel: a drowned expedition's journal describing a river that flows under the glacier to an unmapped source. Someone has already searched the cave — recently. Beat: curiosity overriding instinct; the trap is already sprung.

chapters.title: The Patron of Skarnvik
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Aldous Vey, the town's shipping magnate, offers to buy the journal for triple the salvage fee. His courtesy is a blade wrapped in velvet. Gideon refuses, then finds her gear searched. Beat: first taste of power's quiet menace.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The salvager's daughter, who hired Gideon, confronts her about the cave. Mara knows the legend — her grandfather died in that expedition — but her father's debt binds her to Vey. Beat: two guarded women recognizing each other's cages.

chapters.title: The Journal's Last Page
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The journal names Vey as the expedition's secret financier and accuses him of cutting the team loose to die when they found something at the source worth owning. Beat: the stakes shift from money to murder; Gideon decides to run the river.

chapters.title: Debt of Blood
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vey pressures Mara's father to retrieve the journal, invoking the family debt. Her father refuses — quietly, fatally. Mara finds the workshop ransacked and her father gone. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon and Mara slip out of Skarnvik by night, following the river's gorge. Vey's men are a day behind. Beat: fugitive intimacy — trust built in motion, in shared silence.

chapters.title: The First Rapid
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They run a gorge rapid on a patched raft; Gideon's old skill surfaces, along with the memory of the accident that got her blacklisted — a client she couldn't save. Beat: competence as confession; Mara sees who Gideon really is.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A ranger station blocks the route — the source is legally forbidden. Gideon talks them past using a forged permit, lying fluently, and Mara realizes how easily Gideon bends. Beat: love against duty begins to strain.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Storm-bound in a snow cave, they share their worst nights: Gideon's drowned client, Mara's father. Something unguarded passes between them. Beat: the quiet center of the book; tenderness earned.

chapters.title: Hunted on the Ice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vey's men ambush them on the glacier tongue. Gideon uses a crevasse field to break the pursuit, but takes a fall that costs them supplies. Beat: survival's price made literal — blood, gear, time.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They find the drowned expedition's last camp, frozen mid-flight. Evidence shows Vey's men executed the survivors. Mara's grandfather's body is among them. Beat: grief confirmed; the legend was a cover-up.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. One of Vey's hunters, Torv, catches up alone — and defects, disgusted by what he was ordered to do. He warns them Vey has chartered a helicopter and knows the source's value: a rare-earth deposit worth a nation's ransom. Beat: the enemy's motive revealed; the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The glacier begins to calve early. The river route will close in days, not weeks. Torv's knowledge of the ice gives them one narrow window. Beat: desperation; nature itself joins the pursuit.

chapters.title: The Ice Tunnel
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They enter the glacier's interior river tunnel — the route the drowned expedition took. Gideon must lead through collapsing ice using only sound and rope-craft. Beat: Gideon at the peak of her craft; the guide redeemed by the work itself.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the forbidden source: a cathedral of blue ice over a glowing mineral seam — and the proof of everything Vey buried. Vey's helicopter arrives; he came personally. Beat: awe curdled by dread; the treasure is real, and so is the greed.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Source
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vey offers Gideon full redemption — records cleared, name restored — in exchange for the journal and silence. Gideon hesitates; Mara watches her almost take it. Beat: the book's moral crux — love against duty, price against principle.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vey's men seize the journal; the glacier calves massively, destroying the helicopter and killing Vey's crew. Gideon saves Vey from the ice, and he, unrepentant, tries to kill her anyway — and falls into the crevasse he cut for others. Beat: chaos climax; power devours itself.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wounded, they descend the river as the route seals behind them, carrying the evidence. Torv stays at the source to mark it for the authorities. Beat: exhausted aftermath; survival stripped to its essentials.

chapters.title: Skarnvik Reckoning
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They return and give the evidence to the town and the rangers. Vey's empire cracks; some blame the messenger. Gideon faces the crowd she once feared. Beat: truth as a costly, imperfect victory.

chapters.title: What Redemption Costs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The authorities offer Gideon full exoneration — built partly on Torv's sacrifice and Mara's testimony. Gideon realizes a clean name bought with others' blood isn't the thing she was missing. Beat: the theme resolved; she declines the easy ending.

chapters.title: Moving Water
chapters.summary: Gideon and Mara, shared POV closing on Gideon. They leave Skarnvik together, upstream of their old lives, with no contract and no blacklist — just a river and a choice. Beat: quiet resolution; stopping, for once, costs nothing.
